teamStories.summary: A 29-year-old is the NBA's next breakout star. Miami's Giannis era is already cooked. And so are the Thunder, Knicks and Warriors. Which overreactions are valid?
teamStories.detailText: Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season . After all, small sample size theatre has provided early gems such as: The sky is falling in Oklahoma City , New York and Miami ! The three-guard experiment in San Antonio needs to go! Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball ! Ty Jerome ? Ty Jerome! With those early storylines and more in mind, let's examine 10 popular overreactions to the young 2026-27 season -- and determine which have staying power. ( Note: stats through Tuesday's games .) The Miami Heat will finish with their worst record since 2008. Zach Kram: Not an overreaction For reference, 2007-08 was the last time the Heat finished with fewer than 37 wins, the season that they tanked down the stretch to go 15-67 in a futile attempt to land Derrick Rose in the draft. Merely by the law of averages, the 2026-27 Heat are bound to improve. They've had the seventh-worst shooting luck on offense, according to GeniusIQ tracking, and the second-worst shooting luck on defense. Miami is actually forcing teams into tough shots, but its opponents have been on fire regardless, making 53% of their midrange shots and 40% of their 3s, per Cleaning the Glass. On the other hand, the Heat's offense has been stuck in the mud even accounting for that poor shooting luck, and guard Davion Mitchell is the only role player who looks comfortable playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo . There's time for that to change -- but as of Wednesday, ESPN's Basketball Power Index predicts the Heat will finish the season with just 38 wins. That's already down from 46 projected wins in the preseason, and just one ahead of this historical franchise benchmark. Ben Golliver: Overreaction Let's be clear: The Antetokounmpo era in South Beach is off to an atrocious start. Instead of building off its blockbuster trade for the two-time MVP with a transformative offseason, the Heat lost Norman Powell to the Chicago Bulls in free agency and settled for adding Klay Thompson , who is a shell of his former self at age 36. On the court, it's already clear that the Heat need another proven ball handler and more shooting, and Antetokounmpo needs more time to jell with Bam Adebayo . Despite all those challenges, it's reasonable to give Heat coach Erik Spoelstra and his staff a long runway . Antetokounmpo's need to dominate the ball has clashed with the free-flowing offensive system that Miami utilized in 2025-26, and several veteran players seem to be easing into the new season. Spoelstra is a tinkerer who has conjured winning records from less talented rosters, and he'll be willing to trust his younger options if Miami's offensive struggles persist. It's probably best to withhold judgment until after the Heat's upcoming trip out West. If the Heat can't get right against teams such as the LA Clippers , Sacramento Kings , Golden State Warriors and Utah Jazz , sound the alarm. There is some good news: Antetokounmpo has been very productive in the early going, averaging 27.6 points, 11.2 rebounds and 4.6 assists after missing most of last season due to injuries. The Oklahoma City Thunder 's title hopes are gone without Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace . Kram: Not an overreaction Earlier this week, I went into more depth about the impact of these two long-term injuries on Oklahoma City's title chances. The simplified version: The Thunder's winning formula over the past few seasons has been to combine MVP-level offense from Gilgeous-Alexander with the best defense in the league. The collective loss of Williams, Wallace and Luguentz Dort (via summer trade) bends that second factor out of shape. Yes, centers Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein still form an imposing backline, and Alex Caruso (currently out with an ankle sprain ) remains a singular defensive force. But the rest of Oklahoma City's perimeter rotation is now so thin, with enough defensive questions, that I would be surprised if it won another title -- barring a return from one of those injured starters before the playoffs or a significant in-season trade. Golliver: (emotional) overreaction Yes, it sure felt as if the sky was falling Monday when Thunder general manager Sam Presti announced that Williams and Wallace are out for the foreseeable future with significant injuries . That's no way to launch a title chase. After those injuries and the offseason trades of Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe , the Thunder are down five of their top six players by minutes logged during the 2024-25 championship season. Oof. But there's an awful lot of talent remaining around Gilgeous-Alexander, who has been sensational to start this season. Oklahoma City showed its resolve by beating Phoenix on Monday night, and it's worth noting it was only one win from reaching the Finals last year despite an injury-plagued season and postseason for Williams. Presti has picks and tradeable contracts to invest in stop-gap additions before the trade deadline, but he also has a deep roster that was built for the long haul. Count out the Thunder at your own peril. Ty Jerome will be an All-Star. Golliver: Overreaction Only a jerk would root against Jerome, who looks destined for a career year after surviving countless fits and starts to get here. But the Memphis Grizzlies ' schedule has been about as soft as it gets to start the season: The Jazz look poised to give up 30 points to any opposing guard, while the Warriors' injury issues and the Kings' general dysfunction disqualify them from being quality wins. Jerome is a talented scorer who more than earned this promotion to lead ball handler, but let's check back in a few weeks. The good news: LeBron James and Kawhi Leonard left the Western Conference over the summer, so there are more available All-Star spots than usual. Kram: Not an overreaction Jerome wasn't an All-Star last season, of course, because he played only 15 games. But he has been a star-level offensive player for a while now, even if few people recognized it until he started averaging 30 points. Here are the NBA's leaders in offensive box plus-minus for the 2025-26 campaign: Nikola Jokic Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Ty Jerome Luka Doncic Giannis Antetokounmpo Kawhi Leonard Victor Wembanyama Stephen Curry Jamal Murray Donovan Mitchell It doesn't matter when Jimmy Butler III returns -- the Golden State Warriors are cooked. Golliver: Not an overreaction The Warriors finally got their first win of the season Monday, but their opening week has been disheartening. With Butler, Kristaps Porzingis and several players missing time with injuries or ailments, the Warriors sat Curry on a back-to-back and rolled out a starting lineup featuring Yaxel Lendeborg , Brandon Williams , Will Richard , Gui Santos and Graham Ike on Saturday against the Phoenix Suns . That five-man group -- great fodder for Charles Barkley on "Who he play for?" -- will combine to earn less than $20 million this season. Meanwhile, Butler ($56 million) and Porzingis ($19.5 million) are missing in action. There's no way to overcome that math. Kram: Not an overreaction We finally agree, Ben. I'm not especially surprised by the Warriors' predicament because this seemed like a gap year from the start, due to all their injury issues and the lack of any real upgrades over the summer. (Aside from Lendeborg, who looks incredible as a rookie.) Maybe they can stick around the play-in race because the West looks shallower than usual -- the Jazz might also be cooked if Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr . are out for a while -- but Golden State's most important goal should be setting itself up for greater success in 2027-28. The San Antonio Spurs will kill their three-guard starting lineup by Thanksgiving. Kram: Overreaction I tend to think debates about starting lineups are overblown because of how much teams mix and match over the course of a game; lo and behold, the guard trio of De'Aaron Fox , Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle has shared the court for just 43 minutes across four games this season. And while it's way too early to come to significant conclusions using net rating, it's not as if the Spurs have struggled in those minutes. They're plus-15.4 with that three-guard lineup, according to databallr. If San Antonio's coaching staff believes it needs to keep Fox, Harper and Castle in the starting lineup for intangible reasons, then there's no evidence yet that that's a bad idea. Golliver: Overreaction Spurs coach Mitch Johnson could be headed for a real saga that might take months to play out. Of course, the critical decision is whether to start Fox, Harper or both point guards. But Johnson could also buy time for that duo to work things out by swapping Devin Vassell for Tobias Harris or Julian Champagnie . Given Fox's enormous salary and Harper's potential, San Antonio must exhaust every possibility before shifting one guard to the bench. Sacramento Kings coach Doug Christie won't make it to the new year. Golliver: Not an overreaction There are so many red flags coming out of Sacramento that it's starting to look like an Olympics opening ceremony. Naturally, the central tension concerns rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr . and veterans Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine . The Kings have turned Acuff loose for 93(!) shots in his first four career games with hopes he will develop into a franchise guard, but his more experienced teammates have good reason to wonder whether that's the best approach to winning. Christie is stuck, and Ben Simmons ' preseason Achilles tear made a tough job even tougher. The Kings look destined to be the NBA's worst team, and that level of ineptitude typically prompts a response from owner Vivek Ranadivé. Kram: Not an overreaction The Kings have let go of five coaches since Ranadivé bought the team in 2013. Two firings came at the end of a season (George Karl in 2016 and Dave Joerger in 2019), but the other three came early in a campaign: Luke Walton (2021) in November and Michael Malone (2014) and Mike Brown (2024) in December. That pattern tells me there's greater than a 50% chance that Christie won't make it to 2027. The New York Knicks won't get out of the first round. Kram: Overreaction I predicted before the season that New York would win fewer regular-season games than a year ago, so I can't profess to be surprised by their sub-.500 start against a tough schedule. The greatest on-court problem for the Knicks is their 25th-ranked offense, but I expect a prompt turnaround: They rank last in making just 30% of their midrange shots, per Cleaning the Glass, after ranking fifth at 45% with largely the same roster a year ago. In looking ahead to the postseason, moreover, I would have to see a much larger sample of struggles to consider the likelihood that New York won't be favored in any playoff matchup in the East. The competition will be tougher this year, but the Knicks are proven playoff performers. Golliver: Not an overreaction This one is more about vibes than hard analytics. As is often the case for defending champions, the Knicks have had a challenging opening week schedule filled with marquee opponents. In that context, the 2-3 start really isn't the end of the world. New York was in competitive games against aspiring contenders in the 76ers and Celtics last week and then handed the Detroit Pistons their first loss on Tuesday. But the Knicks' inability to pull out those close games was a reminder of just how charmed their 2026 postseason was from start to finish. Jalen Brunson seemingly hit every big shot he needed to hit, and the one time Brunson didn't come through, OG Anunoby was right there for the one-in-a-million tip-in. Time after time, the Knicks cheated death with second-half comebacks. That doesn't feel like a sustainable formula now that they've got the target on their backs. Owner James Dolan has also operated like a man who is comfortable with one ring rather than desperate to add another. Trying to win back-to-back championships has exhausted younger teams than the Knicks in recent years, so no one should be all that surprised if they run out of gas or encounter season-altering injuries before May. Offseason trades made the Charlotte Hornets ' current roster better . Kram: Not an overreaction (although I'm prepared for Ball to make this statement look silly) We all thought Charlotte's surprising offseason trades were made with an eye toward the future. After all, the franchise dealt two foundational players and their two highest-salaried players in Ball and Miles Bridges . But the Hornets received so much flexibility and so many valuable draft assets in return that the "one step back, two steps forward" approach made sense. We might have been giving the Hornets' present-day roster short shrift with that assessment. Charlotte has a winning record despite receiving zero minutes from its starting backcourt, as Coby White and Kon Knueppel deal with injuries. Brandon Miller appears to have taken a leap after signing a five-year rookie extension. And offseason additions Naz Reid and Grayson Allen , who came to Charlotte as part of the Ball and Bridges trades, have combined to average 36.3 points while making 44% of their 3-pointers. Reid, in particular, represents a meaningful upgrade over Bridges at power forward. Golliver: Overreaction The jury is still out on the Hornets given the injuries you mentioned and their weak quality of competition to date. With that said, the decision to trade Bridges is already shaping up to be one of those moves they will never regret. Charlotte's short-term success will be determined by Miller's ability to consistently flex his muscles as an alpha scorer and Knueppel's comfort handling greater playmaking duties. Beyond that, Hornets ownership must demonstrate a willingness to spend to build around that budding duo. The Ball trade could wind up as a win-win for Charlotte and Minnesota, but at some point, the Hornets will need to prioritize talent acquisition and retention rather than careful cap management. Otherwise, they're spinning their wheels. Walker Kessler should be on Team USA in 2028. Golliver: Not an overreaction Before the season, the Lakers argued that Kessler was worth paying a premium price in draft picks in their summer sign-and-trade with the Jazz because it's incredibly difficult to find centers at his age (25) with the ability to finish plays on offense and credibly protect the paint on defense. Grant Hill, Spoelstra and USA Basketball would be wise to target big men with that exact skill set for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, especially if Joel Embiid , Anthony Davis and James opt not to return after winning gold in Paris. Adebayo, Holmgren, Jackson and Evan Mobley could all be in the mix, but Kessler brings a level of sheer size and physicality that those players lack. Wouldn't it be helpful to have a traditional center to deploy with Wembanyama and Jokic looming as threats to the U.S. dynasty? Kram: Overreaction You cited the Grizzlies' schedule when cautioning about Jerome's hot start. I'll do the same for Kessler, whose two big games to date came against a Warriors team that didn't start a center and a Clippers team with Isaiah Jackson in the middle. That's not exactly Wembanyama- and Jokic-level competition. Kessler does have international experience, as he was a deep reserve for the unsuccessful 2023 World Cup squad. I believe he's on the long list of American big men for 2028, but I would need much more evidence to place him higher in the pecking order. The Chicago Bulls will be the worst team in the East. Golliver: Not an overreaction For all the preseason talk about improved parity this season thanks to the new lottery rules , there are still some pretty bad teams. The Bulls, Bucks and Nets have all looked like viable contenders to finish with the conference's worst record. (And yet, somehow, the Heat have been harder to watch than all of them.) The scary part about Chicago's start is how thoroughly Toronto and Boston thumped the Bulls. While the Bulls want to play fast under new coach Tiago Splitter, they're just getting completely run off the court by good teams. There's obviously no reason to panic if the blowout losses mount: Caleb Wilson should be encouraged to play free and make mistakes, and Chicago's new front office should focus on which of its veteran players look like long-term fits around the promising rookie forward. And is it too early to predict the Bulls will be getting rid of players at the trade deadline? Kram: Overreaction The Bulls rank dead last in offensive efficiency, but I believe that's more a product of bad luck than bad process. According to GeniusIQ tracking, the Bulls rank fourth in quantified shot probability, which accounts for factors such as location, defender distance and shooter talent. But the Bulls have underperformed that shot quality by 11.1%, which ranks last by a mile. For context, the largest gap for any team over the full 2025-26 season was just 1.7% -- so Chicago's shotmaking is bound to improve. That doesn't mean I think the Bulls will reach the play-in tournament or anything so lofty. But I do believe that they'll play more like a typical rebuilding team going forward, rather than losing every other game by blowout margins.

stories.title: Cardinals rookie RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) set to return
stories.summary: Jeremiyah Love is expected to return to the field for the Cardinals on Sunday after missing the past two weeks with an ankle injury.
stories.detailText: TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is set to return to the field Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium after missing the past two weeks with an ankle injury. Arizona coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Love will "be good" to play this weekend and will not have any restrictions on what he can do. "We're never going to put a guy out there that we don't think can obviously benefit the team, benefit, in this case, the offense," LaFleur said. "So, I'll keep it at that. But he's out there for a reason and we expect him to go." Love said the rest was needed and that he feels "pretty good." "It helped me get back to myself," Love said. "So, hopefully, I can go out there and execute." Love said the last two games were the first games he's missed since high school. LaFleur emphasized that the Cardinals won't play a player who's not ready, especially those who touch the football. "If they're not dynamic within their own ability, I mean let's get the next guy up," LaFleur said. "So, I mean we feel good. He feels good enough to go out there and produce and look forward to having him back out there." Love said his ankle injuries this season impacted him "quite a bit." Love explained that his thinks his second ankle injury happened in Week 2 against the Seattle Seahawks . However, there's been a discrepancy in which ankle was injured when. LaFleur has said that Love injured his left ankle earlier this season after spraining his right in the preseason. However, on Friday, Love said he sprained his left in the preseason and his right earlier in the regular season. Either way, Love said for a player like him, having healthy ankles is imperative. "I am myself when I got my ankles," Love said. "I feel like as a running back or as a receiver, a lot of the moves that we do with our ankles and knees and stuff like that, I like to come to complete stops. It impacted me quite a bit." LaFleur said no player is fully healthy at this point of the season, but after resting his left ankle for the past two weeks, Love is "feeling as good as he can feel." Love suffered a right ankle injury in Arizona's second preseason game and didn't practice until Week 1, when he made his NFL debut against the Los Angeles Chargers . He then injured his left ankle early in the season and played on it until Week 5 before missing the next two games. "I just want to go out there and be myself," Love said. "I feel like the past few games, for really the whole season, I haven't really been able to go out there and just feel like myself. "I just feel like I just can't go or I couldn't go out there and just do what I wanted to."

Barkley did not practice Wednesday or Thursday and was a limited participant Friday, but he carries no designation into the game. He entered Week 7 against the visiting Dallas Cowboys with a hamstring injury and had his back lock up on him over the course of Monday's game, forcing him to miss a portion of the second half. He played nine snaps and got the ball every time he was on the field, totaling 71 yards and a touchdown. "I would hope so; I believe I'll be able to," Barkley said when asked after Friday's practice if he thinks he'll play against Washington. "There's one day I'm not going to be playing football. Whenever that is, I don't want to look back and be like, 'I could have given it a chance and I didn't.' It's kind of what I live by. I'm going to try my best to just keep recovering, being smart, but I like playing football, so if I have an opportunity to play, I'm going to try my best to play." With running backs Tank Bigsby , Will Shipley , Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele all on injured reserve, Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell are the Eagles' other backfield options against the Commanders. Philadelphia again will be without its top receivers in DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) as it attempts to end a five-game slide. stories.title: 5 Bills to focus on vs. Ravens
stories.summary: After a week to recharge, the Bills face a perennial AFC contender on Sunday
stories.detailText: The Buffalo Bills take on the Baltimore Ravens this week in what will be the first post-bye week game of head coach Joe Brady’s tenure. Under former head coach Sean McDermott, the Bills were a perfect 9-0 following a bye. Can the Bills continue that trend under a new head man? The week of rest came at a good time for Buffalo, as they were plenty banged-up for their last contest against the Las Vegas Raiders. Thanks to that extra week of rest coming into this game, it appears that the Bills will have some of their top players returning for what should be a tough matchup against a strong AFC foe. Here are our five players to watch this week as Buffalo battles Baltimore. _____________________________________________________________________________ WR DJ Moore After missing Buffalo’s last two games thanks to a flare-up of the same shoulder injury that caused him to miss time against the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots, Moore is trending towards playing this week. He will be a welcome addition to a Buffalo passing game that has been outstanding this season. The Bills rank No. 12 overall in passing yards and No. 17 in passing touchdowns despite coming in at just No. 30 overall in passing attempts. This week, quarterback Josh Allen should be even better than he has been with his top wideout back in the game. Moore has 12 catches for 178 yards and a score on 20 targets this season. In the two games where he’s been able to start and finish the contest, Moore has 11 of those catches for 167 yards and a score. In those two games, Allen totaled 538 passing yards and two scores. Moore opens up the Buffalo passing attack, and thanks to the emergence of Keon Coleman this year, the Bills now have two solid wideouts joining Khalil Shakir at the top of the receiver depth chart. Look for the Bills to ease Moore back into action, but if it’s as tight as I think it will be, expect No. 2 to see plenty of targets in the second half in big moments. WR Khalil Shakir Given Baltimore’s success in stopping the run this season—they’re allowing just 3.8 yards per rush so far—I think the Bills might be wise trying to attack via their “11” personnel grouping more often than through their heavier packages. That means there should be plenty of targets for someone like Shakir, who has taken a bit of a back seat in the early going after serving as Allen’s top target over the last two seasons. Shakir is on pace to catch 62 passes for 821 yards and three touchdowns on 91 targets. Those be his lowest totals in targets, receptions, and touchdowns in a season since 2023, which is when he had Stefon Diggs absorbing the majority of the targets. Shakir is as dangerous as anyone in the NFL in space, and he can operate at all levels of the defense to create mismatches. I like Buffalo’s slot targets—Shakir and tight end Dalton Kincaid—this week against the interior of the Baltimore defense, and I especially like Shakir if the Ravens use safety Kyle Hamilton to neutralize Kincaid. OLB Greg Rousseau After a white-hot start to the season, Rousseau has cooled over the course of the Bills’ last three games. Groot began the year by earning Defensive Player of the Month honors for September, totaling 15 tackles, six sacks, three forced fumbles, eight tackles for loss, 12 quarterback hits, and a pass deflection in Buffalo’s first three games. In the three games the Bills have played since, Rousseau has six tackles, seven quarterback hits, four pass deflections, and zero sacks or tackles for loss. Granted, teams took notice of Rousseau’s play and have responded by devising blocking schemes to neutralize him as a result; however, Rousseau can’t be invisible in the pass rush for Buffalo’s beleaguered defense to turn their performance around. Against Lamar Jackson, who should be set to return from an ankle injury this week, the Bills will need to be sound in their assignments and force their opponents to beat them from the pocket. Jackson is excellent within structure, but he is absolutely devastating when allowed to scramble. Rousseau has always done a great job setting the edge, but he’ll need to play up the elite status of his first three games this week in order for the Bills to come out with a win. DL Ed Oliver I was between Ed and linebacker Terrel Bernard for this spot, and while I think it’s essential for Bernard to perform, I’m really intrigued to see what Buffalo’s defensive line can do with a healthy Oliver back in the fold. If teams want to commit their resources to Rousseau on the edge, that likely means that someone like Oliver will have a one-on-one inside, especially given how good nose tackle Deone Walker has been this season. Oliver has dealt with hip and knee injuries this season, and just as the story of his career has gone, the injuries have prevented him from playing consistently enough to make an impact. Look for Oliver to lasso Jackson in the backfield at some point on Sunday for his first full sack of the season (he notched a shared sack during Buffalo’s 29-26 loss to the New England Patriots). S Damar Hamlin I’ve already outlined the reasons why I think the starting safety spot alongside Cole Bishop should go to rookie Jalon Kilgore instead of the veteran Hamlin, but all signs point to Hamlin being the one to take C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s place for most of the snaps on Sunday. Hamlin is limited in coverage, and while he remains a solid tackler, he’s best suited for special teams work. If he finds himself in one-on-one situations against Mark Andrews, or worse yet, Zay Flowers, the Ravens will capitalize. Perhaps Hamlin’s mental acuity will help to settle the defensive secondary, but I’m more concerned that his lack of speed will lead to some big plays. Baltimore is going to try to find No. 3 and use him to their advantage this week. Just as he’s done for the majority of his career, Hamlin will have to rise to that challenge. Here’s hoping he turns in a solid performance, but don’t be surprised if we see some Jalon Kilgore out there at times, as well.

stories.title: With 10 games left and Ejiro Evero out, what's next for Panthers' defense?
stories.summary: Here are three reasons for optimism as Carolina makes a defensive coordinator change to Todd Wash.
stories.detailText: The Carolina Panthers (3-4) are moving in a new direction on defense following Friday's firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero . On Thursday night, the Panthers lost their second consecutive game, falling 27-19 to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. With Evero now out of the mix, Carolina will look to improve the league's 23rd-ranked defense, which ranks third worst in the NFL against the run through seven games. During the former coordinator's tenure the unit ranked 30th in scoring defense, 28th in pass rush win rate and last in rushing defense, so there's room for improvement heading into Carolina's final 10 games of the 2026 season. The Panthers next play Nov. 8 against the visiting Denver Broncos . Evero's departure is an opportunity to switch things up under coach Dave Canales entering the midway point of his third season at the helm. And given the outlook of the defense and the main characters in it, there are reasons to believe the group can improve in short order. Here are three reasons for optimism as the Panthers change coordinators and switch up their defense entering that Week 9 game: Todd Wash will be the new voice calling plays on defense Carolina will hand the defense to interim coordinator Todd Wash for the remainder of the season. Wash was one of two assistant coaches on that side of the ball who had a coordinator background, the other being secondary coach Renaldo Hill. Wash served as defensive coordinator for the Jacksonville Jaguars from 2016 to 2020. During the 2017 season, Wash oversaw the league's No. 2-ranked defense and helped guide the Jaguars to the AFC Championship Game under coach Doug Marrone. Wash also has a long history with Canales and general manager Dan Morgan. The trio worked together with the Seattle Seahawks from 2011 to 2012, as Wash and Canales were assistants under then-coach Pete Carroll and Morgan worked as a scout in the front office. Wash has a background with several different schemes. His hybrid front in Jacksonville mixed and matched odd- and even-front tendencies with four- and three-man trench groups. Given the Panthers' midseason coordinator switch, Wash might still need to lean on Evero's scheme, but he can toy with the fronts in the weeks ahead. Carolina struggled to rush the passer and stop the run during Evero's tenure, and Wash, a longtime defensive line coach, could try to make the most of his well-paid top-tier talent in the front seven by altering game plans around the base principles of Evero's system so players aren't learning on the fly. Defensive linemen Derrick Brown , Bobby Brown III and Tershawn Wharton have scheme versatility. So, too, do outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips , Patrick Jones II and Princely Umanmielen . Inside linebackers Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke can adapt as well if needed. Injured players will be making their returns The secondary was down to its fifth and sixth cornerbacks Thursday night at Green Bay. Marco Wilson , a practice squad elevation, started the game opposite rookie Will Lee III , who was replaced by Chau Smith-Wade after Lee suffered a hamstring injury midway through the game and was ruled out. Starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) have been out for their league-mandated four games on injured reserve, and they are eligible to return to action once they are cleared to perform. According to Canales, the pair is making good progress with rehab behind the scenes. Their returns would be huge for the defensive backfield and for the unit overall. Phillips, who has missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, should return eventually. It would have been tough for Phillips to return on a short week on Thursday, so the Panthers took it easy on the top pass rusher ahead of their final 10 games. Bobby Brown, who had a hand injury that kept him out of the game at Green Bay, should also be able to return in the weeks ahead. There is some upside with the youthful roster On Thursday, safety Zakee Wheatley (pick No. 151 in the 2026 draft) collected the first interception of his pro career. Rookie linebacker Jackson Kuwatch (pick No. 227) forced his first fumble on special teams. The youth movement in Carolina -- and on defense especially -- should be in full force for the weeks ahead. Wheatley, Kuwatch and other members of the 2026 class have flashed, and now Wash -- who is likely auditioning to be retained as coordinator -- can open the floodgates. Wash has already overseen a defensive line in which second-round pick Lee Hunter has been a mainstay all season. He has also been unafraid to give a quality role to undrafted lineman Aaron Hall early on. Other up-and-comers such as Kuwatch, Wheatley and safety Lathan Ransom (2025 fourth-round pick) could benefit from the switch in perspective from Evero to Wash. The Panthers' front office has invested draft picks in those players -- along with Smith-Wade and Umanmielen -- and with Wash getting the interim tag, the new playcaller could try to spotlight the youth over some of Evero's favorites down the stretch.

stories.title: Panthers relieve Ejiro Evero of defensive coordinator duties
stories.summary: The Carolina Panthers are moving on from defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, the team announced Friday, with defensive line coach Todd Wash taking over on an interim basis.
stories.detailText: The Carolina Panthers have relieved Ejiro Evero of defensive coordinator duties, the team announced Friday. Longtime defensive line coach Todd Wash will serve as interim defensive coordinator for the remaining 10 games of the season. Defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley was also let go Friday. Panthers head coach Dave Canales said team owner Dave Tepper, GM Dan Morgan and EVP of football operations Brandt Tilis were "involved in the process the whole time -- ultimately, this is my decision," Canales said of the call to move on from Evero. "This falls squarely under the responsibilities of the head coach. And so, as I was evaluating it, and looking for what was best for the 2026 Carolina Panthers, this was a decision that we discussed. And weighed in all the factors -- the timing of it, the position of our group -- all of those things to make the best decision going forward." As a result of the changes, outside linebackers coach AC Carter will add defensive line duties with Wash's promotion, and secondary coach Renaldo Hill will oversee the entire defensive back operation following Cooley's departure. The Panthers are also considering adding to the defensive staff given the aforementioned departures, a source told ESPN. Carolina lost 27-19 to Green Bay at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, a game that highlighted many of the inconsistencies that have plagued the defense this season. The Packers racked up 354 net yards and four touchdowns against the Panthers' defense. The group allowed 291 rushing yards and eight total touchdowns in a Week-1 loss to the Chicago Bears and 258 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns in a Week-6 setback against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Through seven games, Evero's defense ranked 30th against the run, ninth versus the pass and 23rd in total defense. The Panthers are also allowing an average of 27.6 points per game, the sixth most per game in the league. Wash previously served as the Jacksonville Jaguars ' defensive coordinator from 2016 to '20. In 2017, Wash oversaw the league's second-ranked defense and the Jaguars made it to the AFC Championship Game. "Just want to see the guys connected," Canales said about his expectations for the defense under Wash. "I want to see them excited about going out there and executing the plan and playing fast and playing the physical brand. "The effort's been there and those things are right, but I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page -- tying in the whole unit. Eleven as one -- do your one-eleventh and being able to execute that way. That's what I'm hoping happens, and for me, philosophically speaking, it starts with the run game. It starts with owning first and second down. And being able to be aggressive and attacking in different ways." Evero, 45, had led the Panthers' defense since 2023 (59 games). He was already on staff when coach Dave Canales was hired in 2024. Despite finishing as the fourth-ranked overall unit in his first season at the helm, Evero's group became the first defense since 1980 to allow 3,000 rushing yards in a single campaign during the 2024 season. Since 2024, Evero's defenses have allowed a league-leading 12 games of 200 or more rushing yards by an opponent. That's six more games than the next defensive units in the category (Giants, Commanders). The unit improved across the board in 2025 following the additions of safety Tre'von Moehrig in free agency and outside linebackers Nic Scourton and Princely Umanmielen in the draft. But the start of 2026 featured extremely mixed results. While the group held standout running backs Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs to pedestrian numbers -- for them -- in impressive wins against the Atlanta Falcons and Detroit Lions , respectively, the defense also had massive letdowns against the Bears, Buccaneers and Cleveland Browns . Evero and Cooley won a Super Bowl together with the Los Angeles Rams

stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on as he walks through the tunnel against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 8 game against the Washington Commanders. The big news is that Saquon Barkley is listed without a game status. He will play on Sunday night. Barkley returned to practice on Friday — albeit in a limited capacity — after being listed under did not participate on Wednesday and Thursday. There’s no question that Barkley wanting to play and help his team try to turn the season around is admirable. But the team should protect him from himself and sit him down if he’s not nearly healthy enough to play and remain in the game. Which is reasonable to think that’s the case considering he wasn’t even able to fully participate in a practice this week! While overcompensating for his hamstring injury, Barkley injured his back on his first rushing attempt in Week 7 and then played sparingly through obvious discomfort the rest of the game. What’s the point of that? What if he gets further injured? That’s not only a setback as it relates to this season, which very well might be cooked anyway, but potentially long-term as well. It could also prevent teams from making offers not only ahead of the NFL trade deadline but in the offseason, too. Even if you’re not of the mind he should be traded at any point, you should want him healthy for next year! I just think playing him is a short-sighted decision with much more downside than upside. The Eagles ruled five players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks did not practice this week ahead of their second straight game missed; the Eagles will once again be without their top two wide receivers. With Covey also out, the Eagles only have four healthy wide-outs on the roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Against the Cowboys last week, Cooper played the most snaps of any Eagles WR while Lemon was right behind him. Despite this, Cooper only saw three targets while Lemon saw eight. The team will probably look to force-feed their rookie first-round pick again in this matchup. To be determined if they’ll look to elevate a fifth receiver from the practice squad. Their options there: Erik Ezukanma, Xavier Gipson (who also has returning experience), and Quentin Skinner. Campbell will miss the first game of his career. Jeremiah Trotter Jr., who was already eating into Campbell’s playing time, will start in his absence. Smael Mondon is the only linebacker on the roster behind Trot Jr. and Zack Baun. Jones has been the Eagles’ top backup cornerback on the outside. His absence might mean that Kelee Ringo (or Jakorian Bennett or Mac McWilliams) is the next man up if Quinyon Mitchell or Riq Woolen miss snaps. The Eagles ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Jakorian Bennett. Bennett fully participated in practice all week. He’s still in his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to activate him from IR in order for him to play on Sunday. They’ll need to open a roster spot to do so. Players notably listed without a game status: Barkley (as previously noted), Zack Baun, Landon Dickerson, Dallas Goedert, Drew Kendall, Tyler Steen, Arnold Ebiketie, Smael Mondon, Michael Carter II, Nolan Smith, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Moro Ojomo, and Marcus Epps . They all appeared on the injury report this week. Nolan Smith is notably set to return after missing Week 7 due to a concussion. Michael Carter II is also set to return after missing the Eagles’ last two games. Hunt and Ojomo will play but they were limited in practice all week. They’re clearly not 100%. stories.title: Jeffery Simmons says calling Caleb Williams "Painted Nails" was "just smack talk"
stories.summary: New Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said his nickname for Caleb Williams two years ago was nothing more than gamesmanship.
stories.detailText: New Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said his nickname for Caleb Williams two years ago was nothing more than gamesmanship. Simmons, then with the Titans, jokingly referred to Williams as "Painted Nails" in an NFL Network interview. He said Friday that he thought Bears fans were "going to crash my Instagram" after that. Now, Simmons, Williams and Bears fans are on the same side after the trade from Tennessee. “ I’ve been a fan of Caleb ,” Simmons said, via Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times . “Of course, being on the other side and having to play against him, I’m not going to tell him that. I’m going to talk as much smack as I can. “But now he’s on my team. Any teammate you ask about me, man, I have my teammate’s back, no matter if he’s on the other side of the ball or not. I’m going to talk the most smack to you when you’ve got a different color jersey on, but when we’re on the same team on Sundays, I go to war for any of my guys in the locker room. I hope Caleb would know that.” Simmons said he and Williams talked after a joint practice in August and again on Friday morning before meetings. Williams doesn't hold the comment against Simmons. “The comments a couple years ago about the nails is all part of my game, with the smack talk,” Simmons said. “I don’t know if you guys have heard, but I’m probably one of the best smack talkers. I talk a lot of smack when I’m on the field. I’m looking forward to being his teammate. We all know what type of player he is.”

stories.title: Hot Take Friday: Super Bears, Super Bowl
stories.summary: With the arrival of Jeffery Simmons, the Chicago Bears can win the Super Bowl. Embrace it, Bears fans.
stories.detailText: NEW ORLEANS, LA - JANUARY 26: Head Coach Mike Ditka of the Chicago Bears gets carried off the field after they defeated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX January 26, 1986 at the Louisiana Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Bears won the Super Bowl 46-10. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hot Take Tuesday is coming at you a few days late, thanks to an illness that had me at death’s door earlier in the week. I’ll spare you the details, but I think I felt about how Jabba the Hutt looks. Wasn’t sure when I was going to surface, but I started ticking up Thursday and Friday and was trying to get back into the swing. It makes it a lot easier to get some motivation to sit down at a keyboard when the Chicago Bears go out and trade for Jeffery Simmons. Let’s say it loud and clear for the Green Bay Packers fans in the back: the Chicago Bears are set up to win a Super Bowl. They have taken their chips and pushed them to the middle of the table. They have placed a bet on Ben Johnson, they have placed a bet on Caleb Williams, and they have placed a bet that they have everything they need to win it all. Guess what? I think they’re right. What’s great about this all-in move is that it’s not a sacrificial all-in move. The Bears are still set up really well for the next few years. The Bears won’t have first-round picks the next two years, that’s true, but if the Bears are as good as I think they are, those picks are probably going to be in the last four picks of the first round; hopefully it will be quite literally the last pick. If the Bears gave up the 32nd pick for Jeffery Simmons, who’s complaining? Hell, they already gave up the 32nd pick once upon a time for Chase Claypool. Draft capital is critical for rebuilding teams; clinging to first-round picks doesn’t matter nearly as much when you are picking in the late 20s or early 30s. It’s time to rewire your brain. I know, first we had to rewire our brains to understand what it was like to have an actual quarterback in Caleb Williams. Then we had to rewire our brains to understand what it’s like to have an offensive genius as a coach with Ben Johnson. Now it’s time to rewire our brains and understand how to operate as a winning franchise. The LA Rams say F them picks. Why? Because trading away picks in the 20s for star players is a far better hit rate on those picks than picking a player. The Rams don’t actually say F them picks. They say F them first-round picks. They always have plenty of day 2 and day 3 picks, and they draft well and find plenty of quality players with those picks. Then they use trades and go out and get the likes of Matthew Stafford, Myles Garrett, Davante Adams, etc. I understand the Rams are having a trainwreck season (for now), but their sustained success over the last several years has been something we’ve all witnessed. If the Bears have the same mindset, I’m all for it. The Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber head coach. The Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber quarterback. The Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber offense. And now, the Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber defense. How good is this defense going to be? That’s hard to tell, but Simmons isn’t just adding an excellent player into the mix. He’s a multiplier. He’s one of the most double-teamed players in the NFL. Which means less attention to the other three linemen, which gives them consistently winnable one-on-one situations. Simmons, despite those double teams, will still make plenty of impact plays each game. And his presence will allow those other linemen to make their share as well. When the line is this far improved, it improves the back seven as well. Devin Bush will stop getting tied down with blockers because they’ll all be blocking Simmons. He will be able to make more plays. The Bears will be able to bring more pressure without blitzing, allowing more defenders to roam the secondary. The Bears will be giving QBs less time to throw, which means less of a chance to expose their weaker coverage players. Everyone on the defense just got better thanks to Jeffery Simmons. Is Ryan Poles done adding? I think there’s a strong chance we see one or two more moves that probably only involve day three picks, but yes, Khalil Mack can be had for a day 3 pick. I would love to see the Bears add Mack, and I would love to see the Bears add a solid CB into their secondary. But even if this is the only move they make, it was one hell of a move. Well done, Ryan Poles. The Chicago Bears have put the league on notice. Their time is now. And as Jake Taylor in Major League said, there’s only one thing left to do… Win the whole f*ckin’ thing.

stories.title: Stop Looking for the Next Ben Johnson
stories.summary: Every Jets coaching search starts the same way. Find the next hot coordinator before anyone else does. Find the next Ben Johnson, the next Liam Coen. It sounds smart. It isn’t. The Jets are 2-5, Aaron Glenn is 5-19, and the team has three first-round picks and well over $100 million in cap space coming […]
stories.detailText: Every Jets coaching search starts the same way. Find the next hot coordinator before anyone else does. Find the next Ben Johnson, the next Liam Coen. It sounds smart. It isn’t. The Jets are 2-5, Aaron Glenn is 5-19, and the team has three first-round picks and well over $100 million in cap space coming in 2027. This is the most important hire the franchise has made in a decade, and the worst thing they can do is treat it like a lottery ticket. Here’s the problem with chasing the next star coordinator: you only know who he is after it works. Coen had one year as an offensive coordinator in Tampa when Jacksonville took him. Johnson spent a cycle turning down jobs before Chicago landed him. Both look like geniuses now. Jacksonville went 13-4 last year and Chicago took the NFC’s No. 2 seed. But at the time, plenty of teams passed on both, and plenty of other “next big things” went nowhere. If you can’t clearly see who that guy is by now, you’re guessing. Guessing on your head coach in the same offseason you draft your franchise quarterback is the definition of stupid risk. So stop guessing, and shrink the job down to the one thing that actually matters: building a quarterback. Not culture. Not a defensive identity. Not a big name who wins ten games around whoever’s under center. The 2027 quarterback is the franchise for the next decade, and the head coach’s job description should start and end with him. The rest of the roster, the line, the secondary, the depth, Darren Mougey has already shown he can fix with picks and cap space. The good news is that QB development is the one thing you can actually check. Shane Steichen called the plays for Justin Herbert’s Rookie of the Year season, for Jalen Hurts’ 2022 jump to MVP runner-up, and for Daniel Jones’ revival in Indianapolis, where Jones was an MVP candidate at 8-2. Dan Pitcher has been in the room with Joe Burrow every day of Burrow’s career. And in college, nobody has a better eye and hand for quarterbacks than Oklahoma State’s Eric Morris. He was Mahomes’ offensive coordinator at Texas Tech, and he found Cam Ward as a zero-star recruit at Incarnate Word and coached him at two schools on his way to becoming the No. 1 overall pick. Now he’s done it again with Drew Mestemaker, a kid who never took a varsity snap at quarterback in high school and is now the top QB on a lot of 2027 boards after developing at lightning speed. Those aren’t projections, they’re track records. You can argue about clock management or a head coaching record, and you should hire around those weaknesses, but you’re not guessing about what these guys do best. And here’s what the hot-coordinator crowd misses: get the quarterback right and the next Ben Johnson comes to you. Coaches chase quarterbacks. The Chargers had Justin Herbert, and when their job opened, Jim Harbaugh took it. A Jets team with a young franchise quarterback on a rookie deal, a stacked draft haul and a GM who knows how to build assets becomes one of the best jobs in football the next time it opens. That’s how you land a star coach: you build the thing star coaches want to coach. The Jets have tried it the other way. They’ve chased the hot name, the culture guy and the defensive mind, and they’ve started over with a new quarterback again and again. This time, flip the order. Hire the coach who builds quarterbacks, draft the quarterback, and let everything else follow. Get that right, and the Jets won’t be hunting for the next Ben Johnson. He’ll be calling them.

stories.title: Ravens QB Jackson to return for Bills clash, calls ankle pain 'bearable'
stories.summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will return to play Sunday at Buffalo, saying the pain in his injured left ankle is "bearable."
stories.detailText: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will return to play Sunday at the Buffalo Bills , saying the pain in his injured left ankle is "bearable." The two-time NFL Most Valuable Player has missed the past three games with a high ankle sprain. He was a full participant in all three practices this week for the first time since he hurt his ankle in a win over the Tennessee Titans 26 days ago. "I feel like I'm no longer a statue," Jackson said after Friday's practice. "I'm able to move around a little better. I can give it a shot." During media viewing of practices this week, Jackson was never spotted running at full speed, but he didn't favor the ankle when jogging briskly. He had his left ankle taped for every practice this week. Jackson wouldn't put a percentage on how he feels, but it doesn't sound like he is at full strength. Asked how the ankle feels compared to last week, Jackson said, "It's better. It's better." Teammates talked this week about how Jackson's return will provide an emotional lift to the team. But the Ravens also made it clear that they can't rely on Jackson to carry the team. Still, Baltimore is a different team when Jackson is on the field. Since he became a full-time starter in 2019, the Ravens are 76-35 (.684) with Jackson, averaging 28 points per game. Without Jackson over the past seven seasons, Baltimore is 7-14 (.333), averaging 17.6 points per game. The Ravens acknowledged they are aware of a rust factor, and they tried to make the practice as close to game-like reps as possible. "I think he'll look like Lamar Jackson," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "Again, I think he's just done such a good job dealing with the injury and doing things to help it get better and get better and get better. And I think now he'll be in a position to be able to play Lamar Jackson football." Jackson acknowledged that he has heard criticism on social media over him missing games because fans tag him in their posts. Asked what he would say to fans who question whether he should play hurt, Jackson replied, "Why would you second-guess me?" Minter and the Ravens have talked about Baltimore reaching a crossroads in the season. After losing two straight games, Baltimore (4-3) has fallen into last place in the AFC North. The Ravens now play at the Bills (5-1), who have beaten Baltimore three straight times in Buffalo. "The sense of urgency is extremely high," Jackson said. "We're trying to get back to where we should be." This season, the Ravens have been inconsistent when Tyler "Snoop" Huntley has filled in for Jackson. In 14 quarters with Jackson this year, Baltimore has scored 14 touchdowns. In 14 quarters without him, the Ravens have scored five touchdowns, including no points in the second half the last two weeks. Last week, it looked like Jackson had a shot at returning but he was ruled out a day before the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals . "I woke up [last Saturday], my ankle was swollen, so that pretty much did it," Jackson said. "I feel like it would've been hard for me to make a decision on the day of the game." Before spraining his ankle, Jackson was playing at an extremely high level. He ranked third in the NFL with 82.6 QBR, throwing six touchdown passes and one interception. At that time, he also led quarterbacks with 144 yards rushing. On Sunday, Jackson faces a Bills defense that ranks 31st against the pass. The last time Jackson missed multiple games in a row was last October. After being sidelined three games due to a hamstring injury last season, Jackson came back to complete 18 of 23 passes (78.3%) for 204 yards passing and four touchdowns in a 28-6 win at Miami. The Ravens have similar high expectations for Jackson. "I think we'll see a great version of Lamar," Minter said.

stories.title: Why the Seahawks are allowed to have five comp picks in 2027 NFL Draft
stories.summary: The Seahawks will be loading up on compensatory draft picks in 2027, but why do they have one more than is usually permitted?
stories.detailText: The Seattle Seahawks technically have just five picks in the 2027 NFL Draft as things stand right now. By the early part of spring, they should have 10 picks after their five compensatory selections are awarded . After the Quenton Nelson trade, one of our commenters brought up that the Seahawks should only get a maximum of four compensatory picks, which is something I want to address and clarify! It’s a partially correct statement but with a caveat. Free agency comp picks max out at four Compensatory picks for free agents do have a limit. Next season, the Seahawks are slated to have comp picks for the following FA departures: Kenneth Walker III Boye Mafe Coby Bryant Riq Woolen Dareke Young’s contract was too low to be classified as a compensatory free agent (CFA) and Seattle didn’t sign a single CFA free agent. NFL rules limit the maximum number of compensatory picks awarded through free agency to four. That the Seahawks were a -4 in compensatory free agents lost is purely coincidence. Even if the Seahawks didn’t retain Rashid Shaheed and Josh Jobe and lost six CFAs while signing none, Seattle would’ve instead been awarded the four highest valued comp picks by round. The Nolan Teasley comp pick is separate Seattle’s fifth comp pick is a 2027 third-rounder for Nolan Teasley, who left the Seahawks assistant general manager role to become the Minnesota Vikings GM. Teasley is biracial— his father is black —and therefore he qualifies as a minority candidate hiring. Under the Rooney Rule, teams who lose a minority candidate to a head coach or general manager position—or, more accurately, a primary football executive—receive third-round compensatory picks over the next two drafts. For the Seahawks, they will get third-rounders from the Teasley hire in the 2027 and 2028 drafts. Those picks are completely separate from the comp pick formula, so it is possible to have five compensatory picks in a single draft. In 2022, the San Francisco 49ers had five comp picks split into two minority candidate hires (the first of two third-rounders for Mike McDaniel, plus the second of two third-rounders for Robert Saleh) and three CFA formula picks. Teasley’s third-rounder is set in stone, whereas the free agent comp picks will be settled into specific rounds at the end of the season.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Jets have a couple of familiar faces in quarterback Geno Smith and guard Dylan Parham, adding some intrigue to the Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 8 matchup on Sunday. To preview the game for Raider Nation, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our friends at Gang Green Nation, and MacGregor Wells was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Jets. Q: Geno Smith had a short and underwhelming stay in Las Vegas last year, but it seems like he’s having a better season this year. What are the reviews on the 2013 second-round pick in his return to New York? A: I think Geno has benefitted from a better situation with the Jets more than anything else. Not that the Jets are some model franchise, but the 2025 Raiders seemed to have a bad offensive line and few options in the passing game other than Brock Bowers, who was hobbled by injuries for a good portion of the season. The 2026 Jets have an average-ish offensive line and multiple weapons to throw to, including Garrett Wilson, 1st-round rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr., who is off to a great start to his career, fellow 1st-round rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq and second-year TE Mason Taylor. For the first time in a very long time, the Jets have a good set of weapons to throw to, and it shows. Geno has been better in 2026 than 2025, but I think that largely has to do with his improved supporting cast. Q: The Jets have another former Raider in Dylan Parham, who signed a two-year, $16 million contract in the offseason. Parham was just an average starter in Vegas, so I’m curious how he’s doing and what he’s brought to the Jets’ offense this year? A: Parham had been doing very well at guard for the Jets before he was injured. He was arguably performing better than any other Jets offensive lineman. However, Parham only played in three games for the Jets before he was injured, and he has missed the last four games, so the sample size is minuscule and the jury is still out on how well he’ll perform in the long run. Q: Garrett Wilson seemingly gave Smith an earful during last Sunday’s loss to the Dolphins, while Fernando Mendoza’s college teammate Omar Cooper Jr. has been very productive in his first two games back from injury. Maybe not right now, but do you think Cooper could eventually take over as the Jets’ No. 1 receiver? What has he shown so far? (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images" data-portal-copyright="Icon Sportswire via Getty Images" /> A: I don’t think Wilson was yelling at Smith. It looked to me like he was yelling at passing game coordinator Seth Ryan. If you take a close look, it looks like Geno is not engaged at all, and Ryan seems to be intently engaged with whatever Wilson was saying. Whether it was Smith or Ryan, Garrett Wilson has not been shy about sounding off when he has felt he was not being utilized properly throughout his career. He is also frustrated over the constant losing he has endured with the Jets every year of his career. It’s possible Wilson will eventually demand a trade, but he doesn’t seem to be there yet. As for Cooper, who knows? I doubt he will ever be a better wide receiver than Garrett Wilson, but I suppose it’s possible. If Wilson is traded at some point, could Cooper be a legitimate WR1 for the Jets? I have no idea. We’ve seen just two games from Cooper, both of which involved 40+ yard receptions. Nobody makes those huge plays on a weekly basis. Cooper won’t either. What will he do if he’s the focus of every team’s top defensive backs? Can he run a full route tree effectively? I don’t know. So far he’s been impressive. We’ll know a lot more by the end of the year, if he stays healthy, regarding his upside and what he can and can’t do well at the NFL level. For now it’s just exciting to have a real weapon opposite Wilson for a change. Q: Speaking of rookies and New York’s first-round picks, what are the early reviews on David Bailey? A: David Bailey has a great motor and a world-class first step. He’s better against the run than advertised, though obviously his pass rush abilities are what pay the bills. He seems to learn quickly. On the downside, for now he’s not a polished pass rusher. He needs to develop the use of his hands and multiple pass rush moves when he doesn’t immediately beat a tackle around the edge with his speed. I think he’s going to be the best Jets pass rusher in decades, but he’s still got a ways to go in his development. Q: Brock Bowers presents a lot of problems for opposing secondaries, and Aaron Glenn typically runs a decent amount of man coverage. So, who do you think Glenn will put on Bowers, or what do you think the strategy will be? A: Let’s be real – the Jets have no answer for Bowers. Few teams do. I’m sure the safeties Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick will try to cover him at times, and the linebackers Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood will take a shot at other times. But the safeties are too small, and the linebackers are too slow. Bowers will get plenty of production against the Jets. The key for the Jets will probably be limiting the other Raiders’ weapons to minimal production.
